title: Solo dev, made a winter train roguelite with AI art + AI-assisted code. Trailer is real gameplay, would love blunt feedback
author: zloy_molo4nik
selftext:
I'm working on a roguelite game where you drive a train through a frozen country with a cold front chasing you. You stop at towns, send the you hero to search buildings, pick up survivors, fight off gangs and between runs you rebuild a refuge.

  
I made the core mechanics a few years ago, then the project just sat in a repo. This year I picked it up again and moved it to Godot from Unity. Continued development with Claude Code which is helping me with the boilerplate code. The art is AI generated. But main UI I made in Figma.

Wanted to bring to life my idea and try myself in game development :)

The trailer is recorded straight out of the engine (Godot’s movie maker), nothing faked or painted over. Even the music is synthesized from code, not a music model.

  
It’s not out yet, no store page. Honestly I mostly wanted to know two things: does the trailer make it clear what you actually do in the game, and does anything scream “AI slop” to you? Be harsh, that’s more useful than nice 🤔 .

  
Looking forward for your feedbacks.   
Thank you

comments.author: Maidforblood
comments.body: This looks cool as hell! Nice!

replies.author: zloy_molo4nik
replies.body: Thanks! Still a lot to polish, but glad it looks fun.
